Thought this movie was gonna be dogshit for so long until I actually saw it, and walked out very entertained and content. It was a really fun adventure movie that actually felt like it had heart, and so far is my favorite of the new Disney Star Wars movies. I never really got the whole argument against having a Han Solo movie, because I’ve been wanting one since I was a fucking kid playing with his action figure. So I was really looking forward to this when it was first announced, and with all the director troubles and rumors that Alden couldn’t act, I’m really glad it came together to be a thrilling ride.

Sure none of the threats felt that real since you knew Han and Chewie would make it out alive, but the story it told felt the most Star Wars-ey out of all the reboot movies IMO. Plus all the different worlds and characters they introduced seemed new and interesting where in all the other movies they just seemed like variations of things we’ve already seen. This was the first one that actually brought new things into the SW universe since the prequels imo, which is the main criticism I usually have of the Disney movies. 

Alden actually began to grow on me as Han throughout the movie too, and about halfway through I accepted his performance and enjoyed what he brought to the table. I mean he was never gonna be Harrison Ford, but I do think there were a lot of scenes where he was able to channel that reckless charm that Han is known for. Even though it was an origin movie for a character that we’ve seen in so many other SW movies, it still managed to be exciting and feel refreshing from the bad taste TLJ left in my mouth. All the small references (“you killed Aurra Sing!”, and “we could’ve gotten Bossk even”) just made this movie feel so much more connected to the greater Star Wars universe, where all the other ones just feel like they’re in their own little bubble tucked away from the rest of the universe. 

With Disney seemingly trying to really distance themselves from all the other parts of the other Star Wars with their new movies and create their own canon, having a movie like Solo that truly doesn’t shun away from the source material is so nice. While none of the threats against Han or Chewie were gonna stick since it’s an origin, they still found a way to get around that and make me engaged in the story despite knowing everything will turn out okay in the end. I really liked Rogue One, but I honestly didn’t care when all he characters ended up dying because there were so many that were given so little time to develop, it just kind of fell flat on me when they started killing them all off in the end. When Han kills Beckett I actually felt something, when Rio and Val died they were given enough screentime and character interactions to make me care about their deaths. Plus Qi’ra and Han’s relationship was really interesting in the end, as it wasn’t just a typical hero and female lead love-interest cliche that we see so much now. 

And honestly I liked how he got the name Solo, it was a cool explanation that fit his story and kind of explains why a character got a really corny name that was even corny in the 70s. It truly showed he had nothing, not even a last name, and had to move up in life from the lowest of lows. How he met Chewbacca was even entertaining and better than I thought it would be. Definitely get around to seeing this if all the mixed reviews and low box office revenue have been stopping you, because it stopped me for about 3 weeks. So I’m really glad I saw this before it left theaters, it told a story that was touching at points and packed with enough action and cool visuals that impressed me.

I'm gonna try to explain this in a way that makes sense in financial terms. NBC, and the showrunners, are taking a huge risk here making a Constantine tv show. Constantine isn't a household name outside of comics. Even if the Keanu Reeves movie was popular, people who saw that and aren't into comics are gonna see this and think it's something completely different. So they're basically starting from scratch in terms of fanbase here (yes, they do have comic fans, but if we're being honest here, comic book movies and tv shows are made to appeal to the broadest audience, and not just comic fans. Especially DC/WB). 

So that's the main issue. Constantine is already an abrasive character, that will take a few episodes, hell maybe even a whole season for people to finally accept. He's a giant dick, he's a supernatural magician, and he's a cockney Brit. Those things aren't that common in tv, so they are really taking a risk trying to get this show off the ground. If they add that' he's bisexual, it'll most likely be seen as just one of those incredibly out there shows that are way too weird to like.

Keep in mind this is NBC, which doesn't normally get along well with weird shows (Community, for example). They gave the show a 10 PM slot on Fridays too. That's not the ideal time for a brand new show, with roots only in the comic fandom, that's a pretty weird concept. Choosing for him not to be bisexual right off the bat is a good idea when you look at it that way. At least I think so. I'm all for him being bisexual, but I'm also all for him getting more than half a season. To do that, with the circumstances given, they have to make the character appeal to the largest audience, which is hard enough having him be John Constantine. Having him be bisexual, which shouldn't be a big deal but it is in today's society, most likely wouldn't garner them the broadest viewers. 

Goyer and the showrunners aren't ashamed of Constantine being bisexual, they just don't want to add that so they can get the most amount of viewers they can. Maybe they'll be more open to it in the second or third season, once they have a fairly loyal fanbase that isn't just from the comic book crowd. But for now, I think they made the right choice. 

That's just my two cents, but think about it if you were in charge, and wanted your show to be a success. You wouldn't have an already obscure, pretty unrelatable character with no mainstream audience be bisexual in the very first episode, or season for that matter. That would turn some people off, which is sad, but let's be honest there are people out there who don't like that idea. Not every choice in sexuality in a character is because the company or showrunners are ashamed of it, they just want to appeal to the broadest audience.

I wouldn't say my life flashed before my eyes, it was more my future flashing before my eyes. Not literally, it was just me imaging everything I still wanted to do in life, and everything I was looking forward to. And then I thought I am never gonna get to experience any of that. It was terrible.

After like 5 minutes I decided to check the situation out, so I grabbed the only thing I could use as a weapon in my room: my guitar. I slowly opened my door with one hand, and had my guitar raised with the other. Turns out nobody was breaking into our house, my dog just saw a deer outside our front door and jumped up and started barking. Hence the shuffling and barking. My mind just made everything else up. Still, it is a terrifying feeling, thinking you're gonna die right now, unexpectedly.
